# Casefile v0.9.0

## Faster Store and workbench

- Completed the Rust speedup and cleanup audit, resolving all 114 recorded findings across HMD-057
  through HMD-068.
- Removed redundant scans, parsing, allocation, cloning, and validation work. Store acquisition uses
  iterative traversal and measured parallelism; narrow reads track their actual dependencies rather
  than being invalidated by unrelated edits elsewhere in the Store.
- Made presentation loading incremental, reused TUI projections and viewport layouts, and reduced
  work during navigation, refresh, and rendering.
- Pushed SQLite filtering into queries and made index replacement transactional. Recognized old
  derived caches rebuild automatically; invalid caches still return actionable errors.
- Added and isolated 59 Criterion workloads, with retained baseline and comparison results.

In the matched isolated comparison, 57 workloads improved and two were inconclusive. Warm TUI
fixture timings improved about 44% for detail rendering, 40% for list rendering, and 17% for
navigation. These are fixture measurements, not guarantees for every Store or machine. The boards
comparison remained inconclusive, with a +3.7% point estimate and a confidence interval spanning
zero. See
[the benchmark report](https://github.com/alsi-lawr/HUMANS.md/blob/v0.9.0/casefile/benchmarks/HMD-068-RESULTS.md).

## Navigation and Codex guidance

- Up/Down and j/k now wrap between the first and last selectable items in lists and boards,
  respecting the current scope and filters. Detail text scrolling, page navigation, and Home/End
  retain their existing behavior.
- Restored Codex skill-usage instructions for the seven Casefile model entries that had disabled
  them. Model selection, effort levels, and specialised review guidance remain unchanged.

## Mutation and transport

- Provider retains each original preview once. Apply operations use its opaque preview ID in the
  same live session, rather than accepting copied preview payloads or fingerprint receipts.
- External edits win when rollback cannot safely restore a file. Incomplete rollback is reported
  consistently across Rust, CLI, MCP, and HTTP; HTTP returns 409 Conflict with affected paths and
  remaining state.
- MCP fails fast and closes the session for oversized or unterminated input frames.
- Replaced the HTTP transport with Hyper/Tokio. Stalled network I/O times out after 30 seconds;
  request body size and connection concurrency remain uncapped. Network timeouts do not cancel
  canonical mutation work.

## Upgrade notes

Provider protocol is now **5**, with explicit typed scope/dependency freshness tokens and ID-only
apply APIs. Upgrade the native executable, plugin, and API clients together; do not mix old and new
wire contracts. Restart the host or open a new session after updating its Casefile MCP registration.

The planning format remains **1**. Existing activated ticket stores and progress logs operate in
place: no ticket migration, rewriting, or reactivation is required. Disposable older SQLite indexes
are rebuilt automatically when their recognized schema needs updating.

The release includes matched Codex and Claude packages with native executables for Linux, macOS, and
Windows on x86-64 and ARM64.
